criticality.studentFacing: You can see that any claim needs evidence to back it up.
criticality.academic: Recognise that a claim needs evidence.

criticality.studentFacing: You can use simple theories to make sense of the data and arguments you meet.
criticality.academic: Interpret data and arguments using basic theories.
criticality.groundedIn: interpret data and arguments using basic theories

criticality.studentFacing: You notice that your own assumptions shape how you read, and you begin to examine them.
criticality.academic: Recognise that one's own assumptions shape one's reading, and begin to examine them.
criticality.groundedIn: for own development: one's own assumptions shape how one reads, and can be examined (Barnett: reflexivity begins)

criticality.studentFacing: You can bring critical skills to the way your subject discusses a topic.
criticality.academic: Apply critical skills within a discipline's discourse.
criticality.groundedIn: applies critical skills within a discipline's discourse (Barnett: critical skills)

criticality.studentFacing: You can see that interpretations are contested, and shaped by where they come from.
criticality.academic: Understand that interpretations are contested and situated.

criticality.studentFacing: You are starting to find an authorial voice of your own, as part of the graduate you are becoming.
criticality.academic: Recognise an emerging authorial voice as part of one's developing graduate identity.
criticality.groundedIn: for own development: an authorial voice is part of the graduate one is becoming

criticality.studentFacing: You can bring sources into your work to support your own point, not just to report them.
criticality.academic: Use sources actively in support of one's own point.
criticality.groundedIn: use sources actively in support of one's own point

criticality.studentFacing: You can build and hold an argument of your own using the latest thinking in your subject.
criticality.academic: Devise and sustain arguments using ideas at the forefront of the discipline.
criticality.groundedIn: devises and sustains arguments using ideas at the forefront of the discipline (Barnett: reflexivity)

criticality.studentFacing: You carry a critical habit into what you do, not only into what you read.
criticality.academic: Extend critical being to professional action, not only to texts.
criticality.groundedIn: for own development: critical being extends to professional action, not only to texts

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can see that not all information is equally reliable.
finding-using-sources.academic: Recognise that not all information is equally reliable.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: not all information is equally reliable

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can narrow your results using filters and limiters such as date, type and subject.
finding-using-sources.academic: Use limiters to narrow search results.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: plan a search: keywords, synonyms, Boolean operators, limiters

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can see that what you already know shapes what counts as relevant, so your searching and your learning grow together.
finding-using-sources.academic: Recognise that one's own knowledge decides relevance, so searching and learning grow together.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: for own development: one's own knowledge decides what is relevant, so searching and learning grow together

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can see that academic searching is exploratory and takes effort, and that feeling unsure early on is normal.
finding-using-sources.academic: Understand that academic searching is exploratory and effortful, and early uncertainty is normal.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: academic searching is exploratory and effortful, and uncertainty early on is normal

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can judge a source against what its type is meant to offer.
finding-using-sources.academic: Evaluate sources against the expectations of each source type.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: evaluate sources against the expectations of each source type

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can see that searching with confidence is part of becoming an independent learner.
finding-using-sources.academic: Recognise that confident searching underpins independence as a learner.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: for own development: confident searching underpins independence as a learner

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can see that information is produced within a wider discussion, and that authority is built up and depends on context.
finding-using-sources.academic: Understand that information is produced in a discourse and authority is constructed and contextual.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: information is produced in a discourse, and authority is constructed and contextual

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You can design a thorough search for an extended project.
finding-using-sources.academic: Design a comprehensive search for an extended project.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: design a comprehensive search for an extended project

finding-using-sources.studentFacing: You treat keeping up with your field as part of your professional responsibility.
finding-using-sources.academic: Recognise that keeping up with a field is part of professional responsibility.
finding-using-sources.groundedIn: for own development: keeping up with a field is part of professional responsibility

presenting.studentFacing: You can see that a talk needs a beginning, a middle and an end.
presenting.academic: Understand that a talk needs a beginning, middle and end.
presenting.groundedIn: a talk needs a beginning, middle and end

presenting.studentFacing: You can read a presentation's marking criteria, so you know what it will be marked on.
presenting.groundedIn: read a presentation brief and its marking criteria

presenting.studentFacing: You can see that your confidence grows from preparing well and from finding your own way of presenting.
presenting.academic: Recognise that confidence grows from preparation and from finding one's own way of presenting.
presenting.groundedIn: for own development: confidence grows from preparation and from finding one's own way of presenting

presenting.studentFacing: You can see that a presentation tests the same skills as an essay, just delivered out loud.
presenting.academic: Understand that a presentation tests the same literacies as an essay, delivered orally.
presenting.groundedIn: a presentation tests the same literacies as an essay, delivered orally

presenting.studentFacing: You can offer your own ideas in a group and listen to what others bring.
presenting.academic: Contribute and listen in a group.
presenting.groundedIn: contribute and listen in a group

presenting.studentFacing: You are starting to see presenting as how you own and assert what you know.
presenting.academic: Recognise presenting as how one owns and asserts one's knowledge.
presenting.groundedIn: for own development: presenting is how one owns and asserts one's knowledge

presenting.studentFacing: You can see that the format, the audience and the medium change what makes a presentation good.
presenting.academic: Understand that format, audience and medium change what a good presentation is.
presenting.groundedIn: format, audience and medium change what a good presentation is

presenting.studentFacing: You can reflect on how you contribute to a group presentation and work to do it better.
presenting.academic: Reflect on one's own contribution to group work.
presenting.groundedIn: lead a group, mediate conflict and reflect on one's contribution

presenting.studentFacing: You adapt how you present and how you lead to each audience and purpose.
presenting.academic: Adapt one's presenting and leading to each audience and purpose.
presenting.groundedIn: for own development: one's presenting and leading are adapted to each audience and purpose
